With the pressures to \SI{393}{\kelvin} in the objective that second liquid is no longer predicted, and at the \res{amp-first-data-measured-splits-transfer-controls} measured states where the first fit predicted it, the AMP model gives one liquid or liquid plus vapor at the measured total pressures (Section~\ref{supp-sec:s-amp-slope}).

At \res{mdea-distinct-descent-states-transfer} of the measured states the measured or assigned pressure lies below the bubble pressure of the model, for example \SI{2.57}{\mega\pascal} against \SI{\res{mdea-zheng-row-5-bubble-pressure-transfer}}{\mega\pascal} at row 5 of the heats of Zheng et al.\ \cite{zhengCO2HeatAbsorption2020} and \SI{0.100}{\mega\pascal} against \SI{\res{mdea-sobrino-example-bubble-pressure-transfer}}{\mega\pascal} for the \COtwo-free densities of Sobrino et al.\ \cite{sobrinoViscosityDensityMeasurements2016} at \SI{393.15}{\kelvin}, and there the model predicts partial vaporization, not a second liquid.

The model overpredicts the pressure of highly loaded, concentrated MDEA: at the highest loading of Zheng et al., 1.18 in 50 wt\% MDEA at \SI{323.15}{\kelvin}, the calculated bubble pressure is \res{mdea-zheng-row-6-bubble-pressure}~MPa against \SI{4.19}{\mega\pascal} measured.

At 30 wt\% and a loading of 0.50, a feed of \SI{1}{\mole} DEA gives a water-rich liquid of \SI{\res{dea-worked-split-water-rich-liquid-density}}{\kilo\gram\per\cubic\metre} and a denser, ion-rich liquid of \SI{\res{dea-worked-split-ion-rich-liquid-density}}{\kilo\gram\per\cubic\metre} that holds \res{dea-worked-split-ion-rich-liquid-share-of-true-moles}\,\% of the true-species moles and \res{dea-worked-split-ion-rich-liquid-share-of-mass}\,\% of the mass.
The sources disagree at these temperatures: at \SI{393}{\kelvin} and 30 wt\% MEA, Jou et al.\ report \SI{46.8}{\kilo\pascal} at a loading of 0.349 and Ma'mun et al.\ \SI{83.6}{\kilo\pascal} at 0.350.
The sources disagree at these temperatures: at \SI{393}{\kelvin} and 30 wt\% MEA, Jou et al.\ report \SI{46.8}{\kilo\pascal} at a loading of 0.349 and Ma'mun et al.\ \SI{83.6}{\kilo\pascal} at 0.350.

At 30 wt\% DEA and 0.50 mol/mol the feed divides into an ion-rich liquid of \res{dea-worked-ion-rich-feed-mole-fraction-supplement} and a water-rich liquid of \res{dea-worked-water-rich-feed-mole-fraction-supplement} of the feed, with densities of \res{dea-worked-ion-rich-density-supplement} and \SI{\res{dea-worked-water-rich-density-supplement}}{\kilo\gram\per\cubic\metre}.

At 30 wt\% DEA and 0.50 mol/mol the feed divides into an ion-rich liquid of \res{dea-worked-ion-rich-feed-mole-fraction-supplement} and a water-rich liquid of \res{dea-worked-water-rich-feed-mole-fraction-supplement} of the feed, with densities of \res{dea-worked-ion-rich-density-supplement} and \SI{\res{dea-worked-water-rich-density-supplement}}{\kilo\gram\per\cubic\metre}.

At \res{mdea-distinct-descent-states-supplement-total} measured states it predicts liquid plus vapor, because the measured or assigned pressure lies below its bubble pressure: \res{mdea-distinct-descents-sobrino-supplement} at 393.15 K and 0.1 MPa \cite{sobrinoViscosityDensityMeasurements2016}, \res{mdea-distinct-descents-bottinger-supplement} at 293.15--333.15 K and 0.5 or 2.5 MPa \cite{bottingerOnlineNMRSpectroscopic2008}, \res{mdea-distinct-descents-zheng-supplement} at 323.15 K and 0.53--4.19 MPa \cite{zhengCO2HeatAbsorption2020} and \res{mdea-distinct-descents-merkley-supplement} at 333.15 K and 1.121 MPa \cite{merkleyEnthalpiesAbsorptionCarbon1987}.

For AMP, the search covers \res{amp-reported-screen-measured-states-supplement} measured states and \res{amp-reported-screen-grid-states-supplement} grid states, all at 1.05 and 3.0 times the bubble pressure of the AMP model, the latter at \res{amp-reported-grid-minimum-stock-supplement} and \res{amp-reported-grid-maximum-stock-supplement} wt\% AMP, the \res{amp-reported-grid-temperatures-supplement} grid temperatures and \res{amp-reported-grid-loadings-supplement} loadings up to \res{amp-reported-grid-maximum-loading-supplement} mol/mol.

At 423 K it lies below the largest tested value without a gap at 1.121, 1.466 and 1.811 MPa alike, and with the fitted temperature law extrapolated the gap appears just above 423 K at all three pressures, so the bound suppresses the calculated gap through the tested temperatures and no further.
The AMP model fits all loaded total pressures to \SI{393}{\kelvin} because a first fit, with fewer of them, predicted a second liquid.

At 373--\SI{393}{\kelvin} it also underpredicts every measured total pressure of the two sources, by \res{amp-first-data-free-hartono-aard-supplement} and \res{amp-first-data-free-tong-aard-supplement}\,\% on average.
